speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when you first noticed this lesion on your leg and if you have had any recent injuries or insect bites in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and anterior uveitis, I need to clarify if you currently experience abdominal pain, diarrhea, or joint pain. Have you noticed any other skin lesions or systemic symptoms like fever or weight loss?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of trauma to the area, and have you noticed any similar lesions elsewhere on your body? I am also interested in knowing if you have been taking any immunosuppressive medications recently.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: ["Crohn's disease", 'Type 2 diabetes mellitus', 'Hypertension', 'Treated for anterior uveitis 8 months ago'] Social history: Recently returned from a visit to Wisconsin 2 months ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of Crohn's disease and the classic presentation of a painful ulcer with undermined violaceous borders following minor trauma, this is highly suggestive of Pyoderma Gangrenosum. I would like to confirm if the pain is disproportionate to the size of the wound and if you have noticed any similar lesions developing after other minor injuries.
